items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: It depends on the project: a landing page usually takes one to two weeks, a visual identity two to four, and a full website three to six. We agree on a clear timeline with milestones before we start.

We set the budget after the discovery session, based on the size of the project and the services you need. You get a detailed quote in Algerian dinars before any commitment, and payment is split into milestones.

items.q: What do I need to get started?
items.a: Knowing your goal and your audience is enough. If you have material (logo, photos, copy), send it over; if not, we help you prepare it during discovery.

items.q: Can I order just one service?
items.a: Yes. You can order a single service, such as a landing page or a logo, and add others later. We make sure everything we design stays consistent with your identity.
We hand over every file and admin access, and stay with you for a period after launch to fix anything that comes up. Monthly maintenance or ongoing content management can also be arranged.

faq.q: How much does a website cost?
faq.a: It depends on the number of pages and features (shop, booking, several languages). After the discovery session you get a detailed quote in Algerian dinars, with no commitment.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: A business website usually takes three to six weeks, depending on the amount of content and how quickly reviews come back. We agree on a timeline with milestones first.

faq.q: Can I edit the content myself after launch?
faq.a: Yes. We set up an easy way to change text and images, and hand you a short guide to running the site.

faq.q: Do you handle the domain and hosting?
faq.a: We help you choose the right domain and hosting and connect them; both stay in your name.

nakhla.title: Nakhla Dates: an identity and a shop that take Souf dates further
nakhla.lead: A family brand of Deglet Nour dates that wanted to sell beyond the region without losing its local character.

challenge.title: A great product, and an image that didn’t say so.
challenge.situation: The dates sold locally in boxes with no clear identity, and orders from other regions arrived by message and got lost in conversations.
challenge.goal: The owner wanted a customer who had never met him to trust the brand, and to order easily from anywhere.

approach.title: We built the identity around the palm, and made ordering a single step.
approach.text: The palm symbol and oasis-inspired colours became the base for boxes, posts and the website. The shop was designed for mobile first, with a page per product and orders going straight into one sheet.
approach.caption: The identity board with its colours and type, and the shop on desktop and mobile.

nakhla.result: A brand customers recognise at first glance, and a shop that takes orders from other regions without lost messages.

basma.title: Basma Dental Clinic: a page that books appointments on its own
basma.lead: A dental clinic that wanted fewer calls, and patients able to book from their phone at any time.

challenge.title: The phone rang all day.
challenge.situation: Every appointment was booked by phone, the front desk was always busy, and anyone calling after hours was lost.
challenge.goal: The clinic wanted one clear page where a patient books in a minute.

approach.title: A one-step form, and everything else in its service.
approach.text: We ordered the page from reassurance to booking: services, the team, then a short form with name, phone and preferred time, followed by an instant confirmation.
approach.caption: The page on mobile, and the one-step form.

basma.result: Easier booking for patients, more time for the front desk, and appointments coming in even after hours.

rimal.title: Rimal Café: content with a consistent look, every week
rimal.lead: A café in El Oued that wanted an account that felt like the place and brought people in.

challenge.title: An active account with no personality.
challenge.situation: Posts were random photos in different colours and fonts, and posting stopped whenever the team got busy.
challenge.goal: The owner wanted people to recognise the café from its posts before they ever visited.

approach.title: Sand-coloured templates, and a monthly plan that keeps going.
approach.text: We designed post and story templates in the café’s colours, and a monthly plan mixing offers, products and moments in the place, plus short animated clips.
approach.caption: The post grid with the new templates, and frames from the monthly plan.

rimal.result: An account with a consistent look and regular posting that introduces the café before the visit.

souf.title: Souf Travel: desert tours in three languages
souf.lead: A desert-tour agency welcoming visitors from Algeria and abroad, that wanted a site everyone could understand.

challenge.title: Visitors from many countries, and a site in one language.
challenge.situation: The agency relied on an Arabic-only Facebook page, and the team explained every tour by message in different languages.
challenge.goal: It wanted a site presenting tours clearly in Arabic, French and English, and taking booking requests.

approach.title: Pictures first, then tour details in the visitor’s language.
approach.text: We built a page per tour with duration, programme and what the price includes, an easy language switch and a simple booking form.
approach.caption: A tour page on desktop, and the language switch.

souf.result: Visitors understand each tour in their own language and book directly, and the team spends less time explaining.

zayn.title: Zayn Store: orders that move on their own
zayn.lead: A small online shop that handled orders by hand between the website, a sheet and messages.

challenge.title: Every order went through copy and paste.
challenge.situation: Each order was copied from the site into a sheet, then sent to delivery by message, so orders were delayed and sometimes lost.
challenge.goal: The owner wanted to see every order in one place, and the team alerted straight away.

approach.title: We connected the existing tools instead of replacing them.
approach.text: We mapped the order flow, then connected the site to a single sheet, an instant team alert and a weekly report that builds itself, with a short training and a written guide.
approach.caption: The order workflow map, and the alert the team receives.

zayn.result: No more lost orders, and a team that knows what is waiting each morning without compiling it by hand.

nour.title: Nour Academy: a one-minute video that explains enrolment
nour.lead: A training centre that wanted fewer repeated questions about how to enrol in its courses.

challenge.title: The same questions, every day.
challenge.situation: The team answered the same questions about enrolment and payment daily, and long written explanations went unread.
challenge.goal: The academy wanted a short explanation anyone could follow the first time.

approach.title: A three-scene story, one character and a simple rhythm.
approach.text: We wrote a short script and drew the storyboard, then animated the character and elements in the academy’s identity and delivered a version for each platform.
approach.caption: Frames from the video, and the timing strip.

nour.result: A clear explainer that is easy to share, and fewer enrolment questions for the team.

meta.description: How the Sahem Studio website collects, uses and protects your data.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.draft: Draft: the final text is reviewed by a specialist before launch.

sections.title: What data we collect
body: When you send the “Start your project” form we receive: your name, your email or phone number, how you prefer to be contacted, the services you chose, your budget range, the approximate timing, and what you write about your idea.
We don’t ask for sensitive data, and we collect nothing else through the website.

sections.title: Why we collect it
body: We use this data only to reply to your request and prepare a first plan for your project. We don’t use it for advertising, and we don’t send you marketing emails without your consent.

sections.title: Where it is kept, and for how long
body: Your request arrives in the studio’s mailbox. We keep it for as long as needed to follow up on your request, and delete it if it doesn’t become a project within a reasonable time.

sections.title: Who we share it with
body: We don’t sell your data or share it with anyone for their own purposes. Technically, it passes through services we rely on to run the website: hosting (Vercel), email delivery (Resend) and the studio’s mailbox (Google).

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can ask to see, correct or delete your data at any time by emailing us at the address below, in line with Algerian Law No. 18-07 on the protection of individuals in the processing of personal data.

sections.title: Cookies
body: The website currently uses no tracking cookies and no analytics. Your browser only keeps your choice of light or dark mode, and it stays on your device.

sections.title: Contact us
body: For any question about your data, email us at {email}.
